question: Can native split partials remain internally consistent while fresh K/V is persisted by one GQA owner and merged exactly once in the final split-state reducer?

cache_first_divergence.finding: The failed runner passed stock_cache[:,0/1] with HND shape [page,head,entry,dim] directly to vLLM reshape_and_cache_flash, whose pinned source indexes its tensor as [page,entry,head,dim].
cache_first_divergence.amendment: The successor runner supplies stock_cache[:,0/1].transpose(1,2), an NHD-ordered ABI view over unchanged HND storage.
cache_first_divergence.director_tentative_blockidx_hypothesis: falsified: pinned decode.cuh launches grid.y=num_kv_heads and sets kv_head_idx=blockIdx.y

output_first_divergence.finding: The failed OutputTransform amended normalized tmp_v with fresh V but did not amend st.m/st.d, so tmp_s remained prefix-only LSE. The first native VariableLengthMergeStates consumer therefore received a mismatched (V,LSE) state.
output_first_divergence.amendment: The successor leaves every partial OutputTransform native and inserts the fresh state only after all partial (normalized V, base-2 LSE) states have been merged.

mechanism: The tail split masks the stale final cache row and otherwise emits untouched native normalized partial V plus base-2 LSE.
One final reducer work item owns each (request,Q-head). It merges all native partials, computes the mapped fresh QK score, and merges (fresh V,fresh score*log2e) exactly once.
KV head is qo_head/2. Only qo_head%2==0 persists fresh K/V, giving exactly one cache owner for each of 16 KV heads per request.
The reducer writes the final output/LSE and the cache owner writes the exact HND physical slot.
